about: Which launch monitors can feed the game, and how. The game listens on TCP 921 and speaks GSPro Open Connect v1 (the role GSPro's Open API plays), so a connector that sends shots to GSPro's Open API can send them here when GSPro is closed. Foresight GC units come in through the built-in Foresight bridge instead. Read by the game (GET /api/launch-monitors, the connection wizard), by tools/arcade-dev/launch-monitors-doc.mjs (docs/launch-monitors.md), the README and the website. Every claim has a source; 'confirmed' means official documentation or source code that was read, anything else is a report.

connectors.name: MLM2PRO-GSPro-Connector
connectors.facts: No heartbeat. Waits 2 s for any reply to a shot, sends the same payload once more, then disconnects. Reads Player.Club of every 201. Spells BackSpin "Backspin". Looks for GSPro's window when the address is local.

connectors.name: gsp-r10-adapter
connectors.facts: One heartbeat on connect with "APIVersion", ShotNumber 0 and null BallData. Strict reply parsing: Code a number, Club from a fixed list, Handed RH or LH. Two replies in one read must be back to back with nothing between.

connectors.name: gspro-garmin-connect-v2
connectors.facts: No Units key. One reply object per read. Target fixed at 127.0.0.1:921.

connectors.name: PiTrac
connectors.facts: Pretty-printed objects with a newline after each. A heartbeat (ShotNumber 0, ready, ball detected) on connect and on change. Putter mode on Club PT.

connectors.name: OpenFlight
connectors.facts: A heartbeat every 5 s when idle, with zeroed ball data present. Applies the Club of every 201. Resends a shot after a dropped link.

connectors.name: squaregolf-connector (read through a fork)
connectors.facts: Newline after each object. A ready status after connecting, with false flags left out. Ball data and club data of one shot as two messages. Acts on the exact Message text "GSPro Player Information".

connectors.name: MLM2PRO-BT-APP
connectors.facts: Keys spelled DeviceId, ApiVersion, Hla, Vla. Reads replies split on newlines only: two objects in one read are both lost. Arms the launch monitor on a 201 unless its DistanceToTarget is 0. Sends misreads with a speed of 0.

connectors.name: GSPro4OSP
connectors.facts: Arms the launch monitor only on a 201 whose DistanceToTarget is not 0.

connectors.name: golfsim-connect
connectors.facts: Waits up to 1.5 s for a reply to everything it sends. A reply whose Message contains "heartbeat" is not counted as a shot's.

fixed.gap: Keys were matched exactly, so "Hla" / "Vla" / "Backspin" / "DeviceId" / "APIVersion" were not read: a shot from such a connector arrived with no launch angles.
fixed.fix: Every key of the specification is matched without regard to case; numbers sent as strings are read as numbers.

fixed.gap: A real shot that also carried IsHeartBeat: true was thrown away as a heartbeat.
fixed.fix: Ball data with a speed is a shot, whatever else is flagged.

fixed.gap: A "shot" with a speed of 0 (a misread) was passed on to the game.
fixed.fix: Acknowledged with a 200, never played (event: ignored).

fixed.gap: Club data sent on its own after the ball data was treated as a status message, which switched the ready light off.
fixed.fix: Acknowledged, reported as its own event (club), and the ready state is left alone.

fixed.gap: The ready and ball-detected flags were read from status messages only; most connectors send them on heartbeats.
After the greeting, a 201 carried only what had changed, so most had no Club. One connector reads Player.Club of every 201; others treat a missing club as a change of club.
fixed.fix: Every 201 is the whole player (Handed, Club, DistanceToTarget). OpenFlight, which applies every Club it is sent, still gets only what changed.

fixed.gap: A 201 could carry DistanceToTarget 0 (the greeting always did). Two connectors read that as "GSPro is in its menus" and do not arm the launch monitor.
fixed.fix: DistanceToTarget is always a whole number of at least 1.

fixed.gap: A club the game could not express as a GSPro code went out as typed; connectors with a fixed list of codes drop the whole message.
fixed.fix: Anything off GSPro's list goes to its nearest code (AW to GW, a loft to its wedge, a 1-wood to DR).

fixed.gap: Two replies could leave in the same instant (the greeting and the first distance update, an acknowledgement and a player update). Connectors that read one object per packet lose both.
fixed.fix: One object per write, at least 75 ms apart; player updates waiting in line are merged.

fixed.gap: A stray closing brace or other noise between objects wedged the stream until 64 KB had gone by.
After "port in use" the server could not be started again without restarting the game.
fixed.fix: start() can be called again; the game retries by itself every 3 seconds and reports the state.

open: The exact Message text of GSPro's 200 reply is not in the specification. The game sends "Shot received successfully" (the specification's description of code 200); two connectors' sources suggest GSPro says "Ball Data received". No connector that was read depends on it.
Whether GSPro answers heartbeats is disputed. The game does ("Heartbeat OK"); no connector that was read is harmed by it.
Codes 202 ("GSPro ready") and 203 ("GSPro round ended") are not in the specification and are not sent.

The game sends Club PT only when the player picks the putter. Connectors that switch a launch monitor into a putting mode on PT (Square, PiTrac, the MLM2PRO connector's webcam putting) are therefore never told that the ball is on the green.
Units "Meters" is not handled: ball speed is taken as mph whatever Units says. BIRDIE_SPEED_SCALE corrects a connector that sends metres per second.
The game accepts more than one connector at a time; GSPro reportedly accepts one.

roadmap.answer: Yes, in part. GSPro Connect is a set of device drivers: for each launch monitor it knows how to find the unit and read its shots. An open-source project can do the same for units whose protocol is published or already has an open-source implementation, and for the open-source launch monitors. It cannot for units that sit behind a maker's SDK licence, an NDA or encryption. Two things are worth knowing first. One: an open-source tool of this kind already exists. flighthook (MIT / Apache-2.0) talks to the Mevo+ family, the Garmin R10 and the Square Omni directly and forwards their shots as an Open Connect client to any address, so working with it is cheaper than rebuilding it. Two: the game's Foresight bridge already is a direct connection of the modest kind, built from what the maker's own connector does in the open.

items.family: Uneekor (EYE XO, XO2, EYE MINI, EYE MINI LITE, QED)
items.approach: The VIEW watcher that already ships with the game: test it, then show its status in the game
items.what: The code exists in this project (tools/uneekor-watch.js, MIT): it follows VIEW's ShotData folder, and the desktop game starts it when that folder is on the PC. No protocol work, no SDK. Missing: one Uneekor owner to confirm units and left/right, and a status panel in SETTINGS > LAUNCH MONITOR like the Foresight bridge has.

items.approach: Nothing to build: test and document
items.what: Both already send Open Connect to a typed address. The work is a test on real hardware with their communities, which moves them to Tested.

items.approach: A built-in reader of its published local API
items.what: OpenLaunch documents a receive-only local API: JSON over TCP and WebSocket, found by mDNS. The developer guide and examples are Apache-2.0. Port numbers and the message schema still have to be read from the guide.

items.approach: A local listener for the Garmin Golf app's E6 Connect setting (TCP 2483), later Bluetooth
items.what: Two open-source connectors (gsp-r10-adapter, MIT; gspro-garmin-connect-v2, MIT per its package.json) accept the Garmin Golf app's E6 Connect stream on TCP 2483: a network listener, no Bluetooth code. Direct Bluetooth is also implemented in the open (gsp-r10-adapter, flighthook) but needs a Bluetooth stack in the game.

items.approach: A local HTTP listener for cam-putting-py (port 8888)
items.what: cam-putting-py (GPL-3.0; protocol facts only) posts each putt as JSON to http://127.0.0.1:8888/putting. Accepting that gives every launch monitor that cannot read putts a putter.

items.approach: Read the GC2's text protocol over USB or a Bluetooth serial port
items.what: The GC2 sends plain KEY=value text (SHOT_ID, SPEED_MPH, ELEVATION_DEG, AZIMUTH_DEG, SPIN_RPM, BACK_RPM, SIDE_RPM). Two open projects show it, neither with a licence file, so a reader has to be written from the protocol facts. Needs serial or USB access from the game and a GC2 owner to test.

items.approach: Use flighthook; a built-in driver only if it proves necessary
items.what: The protocol (binary, TCP 5100 on the Mevo's own Wi-Fi) is reverse-engineered in ironsight (Rust, MIT or Apache-2.0, pre-1.0) and used by flighthook. A port to this game is possible but fragile against firmware updates; neither project may be used to unlock paid features.

items.approach: Use flighthook; a built-in Bluetooth driver later
items.what: The Omni's Bluetooth protocol is implemented in allsquare (Rust, MIT or Apache-2.0). Needs a Bluetooth stack in the game. The older Square Home connector's repository was taken down after a copyright claim: do not build on it.

Open implementations exist (GPL-3.0 and MIT), but each needs a token from Rapsodo's online service and third-party access switched on in Rapsodo's app. A built-in driver would depend on that service and its terms.
No SDK and no open implementation of the wire protocol. The only route is a closed-source plug-in that loads inside SkyTrak's own app.

items.family: Foresight GC3 / GCQuad / GCHawk / Bushnell Launch Pro (direct)
items.what: No public SDK and no open protocol. Foresight's SDK is licensed to partners. The bridge, which uses the owner's own GSPro connector, is the way in.

items.family: Garmin R50, Full Swing KIT, TrackMan, ProTee VX, GolfJoy, VTrack, TruGolf, Uneekor (direct to the unit)
items.what: Private links to GSPro Connect, partner credentials or encryption (R50, as reported), SDKs under NDA (TruGolf, as reported), or nothing published at all. Garmin's Golf API is for selected partners and carries a licence fee.

notes: Not on the roadmap, on purpose: taking GSPro's connector apart, speaking its private protocol, or using keys taken from it. GSPro's terms forbid reverse engineering and unauthorised methods of interacting with its services.
A connector launcher is cheaper than any driver: the wizard could start the chosen community connector with the right address already filled in.
